He took it for a girl's idle mischief and said nothing, since his own father disliked complaints. On the fourth rent day his father asked to see the shop's account book. Hedwig's father went pale and reached for the drawer, but Hedwig was quicker; she set the book on the counter herself, opened to a page in her own neat hand, and stepped back to the clocks. items.passage: Brine and coal smoke: that was the smell of the crossing on the salt flats east of Manchester, where my father ran the little ferry over the brine channel for thirty years. Every April a passenger named Josiah bought two tickets and rode alone, standing at the stern with his hat in his hands, and he left the second ticket tucked into the rail. My father punched both without a word and never asked whose the second one was. The year after my father died, Josiah came on the usual morning and said, "Good day, Miss Mabel," as if nothing had changed. I told him the ferry was closed for repairs to the engine, which was true. I had booked those repairs myself, for that exact week, in January. That afternoon I rowed him across in my father's old skiff, the slow way, with the oars creaking in their locks, and on the far bank I took two tickets from my coat and punched them both.

### lit40-hard-03-073 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose · 요청 난이도 hard · hard 기준: 요지가 한 사건이 아닌 두 사건의 관계이며, 오답이 모두 지문 사실과 양립하는 부분 요지·인과 뒤집기다
[지문]
Dry leaves filled the stone basin of the fountain in our courtyard in Taipei, and every autumn Baoyu came to argue with me about them. He was my father's oldest friend, and he arrived each October with a rake, insisting that the leaves be burned, while I insisted they be left for mulch. My father had sailed for Fujian when I was nine and had sent two letters since. Baoyu never spoke of him. We argued about leaves for six autumns, loudly enough that the neighbors leaned out of their windows. One year he brought a small tin box along with the rake and set it on the fountain's rim; I did not open it, and he did not mention it. The seventh October he did not come. A boy brought the rake and the tin box to the gate with a note in Baoyu's hand: the leaves are yours to decide now. Inside the box were my father's letters to him, thirty of them, every one asking about me.

B) An old family friend keeps up a garden custom after the narrator's father departs.
C) A box of letters shows that the narrator's father wrote more often than she knew.
D) The narrator's refusal to burn the leaves is what leads Baoyu to stop visiting.

On the ninth day, the date written in pencil on the back of the cedar plank she had chosen for me, she declared the frame finished, though I could still see a gap at one joint.
